trends: Today's tech landscape is significantly shaped by the rapid evolution of AI, particularly around the themes of reliability, explainability, and the increasing sophistication of autonomous agents. There's a strong push for 'AI that doesn't lie,' emphasizing data quality, bias mitigation, and robust model evaluation. Concurrently, the rise of agentic AI is evident, with agents becoming more self-managing, integrating into development environments, and automating complex workflows. This trend brings with it a focus on effective agent interaction – preferring structured directives over ambiguous prompts – and the crucial need for continuous monitoring and feedback loops to prevent 'agent skill drift.' Underlying these advancements are ongoing concerns about security vulnerabilities (both legacy and AI-induced privacy issues), as well as a growing awareness of the hidden costs of AI tools, such as excessive resource consumption and their impact on developer well-being and productivity. Overall, the emphasis is on building smarter, more reliable, and sustainable AI-powered solutions that genuinely enhance human capability without adverse side effects.

ideas.title: LocalDev Agent Orchestrator with Scripted Directives
ideas.description: Inspired by the autonomous capabilities of `agent-autoloop` and the AI integration into development environments like `roblox-studio-mcp`, this project creates a local orchestrator for AI agents. It will accept structured script files (e.g., YAML, Python) as deterministic directives for common development tasks such as code refactoring, test generation, documentation updates, or initial project setup. The agent will execute these tasks autonomously, interacting with the local file system and potentially integrating with an IDE via LSP or custom extensions. A key feature will be its 'only bother you when stuck' mechanism, where the agent prompts the developer for intervention only when encountering explicit logical blocks or unresolvable errors, promoting efficient human-agent collaboration. This moves away from ambiguous natural language prompts towards more reliable, scripted AI-driven development.
tech_stack: VS Code Extension API (or similar IDE integration)
Ollama/Transformers (for local LLM integration) or OpenAI/Claude API
ideas.source_inspiration: agent-autoloop, roblox-studio-mcp, Don't Write Markdown Files for Your Coding Agent. Write Scripts., Agent Skills Drift
steps: Design a structured directive format (e.g., YAML with 'action' and 'parameters' fields for file operations, command execution, or LLM calls).
Implement a core Python agent loop to parse directives and execute corresponding modules (e.g., file I/O, subprocess execution).
Develop a basic IDE integration (e.g., VS Code extension) to send context (active file, selection) to the agent and receive proposed changes.
Integrate a local LLM (e.g., via Ollama) or an external API (OpenAI/Claude) to interpret higher-level directives and generate code/text based on context.
Implement an 'intervention' mechanism that pauses the agent and notifies the user for critical decisions or unresolvable issues, requiring explicit developer approval.
Build a simple CLI for managing agent tasks, viewing logs, and manually triggering directive execution.

ideas.title: TrustyML: Conformal Prediction & Bias Reporting Dashboard
ideas.description: Inspired by `predictorlab`'s emphasis on 'ML that doesn't lie,' conformal intervals, and leakage guard, this project is a web-based dashboard designed to enhance the trustworthiness and ethical considerations of machine learning models. It will allow users to upload model predictions, ground truth data, and optionally feature data. The dashboard will then compute conformal prediction intervals (quantifying prediction uncertainty), detect data leakage post-training, and provide comprehensive reports on class imbalance issues (referencing `imbalanced-dataset-sampler`) and potential biases across different demographic or sensitive attribute groups. This tool will equip data scientists and developers with actionable insights to build and deploy more reliable, fair, and transparent AI systems.
ideas.source_inspiration: predictorlab, imbalanced-dataset-sampler, Claude Code sends your email address to websites (highlights privacy/trust concerns in AI)
steps: Set up a Python backend (Flask/FastAPI) to handle data uploads and expose API endpoints for analysis.
Develop a data ingestion module that processes uploaded CSV/JSON files containing model predictions, true labels, and feature data.
Implement a Conformal Prediction module to calculate prediction intervals and confidence scores for classification and regression tasks.

Create a bias detection module to analyze model performance across different sensitive attribute groups (if provided) and report on metrics like accuracy parity, F1-score parity, and false positive rates.
Design and build a React frontend with interactive dashboards to visualize:
Conformal prediction intervals (e.g., actual vs. predicted with error bands).
Class distribution and the impact of rebalancing strategies.
Bias metrics and fairness indicators across different groups.
Implement basic authentication and data persistence (e.g., SQLite) for managing multiple models and datasets.

ideas.title: AI Carbon Footprint & SSD Health Tracker
ideas.description: Directly addressing the concerns raised by 'Codex Was Torching Your SSD,' this project develops a lightweight, cross-platform background application. It monitors system resources (CPU, GPU, RAM, disk I/O, and crucially, SSD write amplification/health metrics) specifically focusing on processes related to AI/ML tools (e.g., local LLMs, AI coding assistants). The tracker provides real-time metrics, logs historical data, and can alert the user when resource usage or SSD wear exceeds predefined thresholds. This helps developers prevent silent hardware degradation, understand the environmental cost of their AI workloads, and foster more sustainable AI development practices.
tech_stack: Flask/FastAPI (for local web UI) or PySide/Tkinter (for desktop GUI)
ideas.source_inspiration: Codex Was Torching Your SSD and Nobody Noticed for Months, Butter Scraped Over Too Much Bread (hidden costs, developer fatigue)
steps: Develop a Python script using `psutil` to monitor system-wide CPU, RAM, disk I/O (reads/writes) and identify specific AI-related process resource usage.
Integrate with `pynvml` (for NVIDIA GPUs) or `roc-py` (for AMD GPUs) to capture GPU usage, memory, and temperature.
Implement SSD SMART data parsing (if possible for common SSDs) or use `psutil`'s `disk_io_counters` to estimate write activity and potential wear.
Create a background service or daemon in Python that periodically collects these metrics and logs them into a local SQLite database.
Build a simple user interface (either a local Flask/FastAPI web server serving static HTML/JS or a basic PySide/Tkinter GUI) to display real-time and historical resource usage.
Add configurable alert thresholds for key metrics (e.g., 'if SSD writes > X GB/day', 'if GPU temp > Y C for > Z minutes') and implement desktop notifications or log alerts.

quick_actions: When using AI coding assistants or agents, experiment with structuring your requests using explicit code snippets, function definitions, or formal instructions within your prompts to guide the agent towards deterministic actions. (Instead of just 'refactor this,' try 'refactor function X to adhere to Y pattern, ensure Z side effects are preserved by adding A, B, C steps.')

Dedicate 15 minutes each week to actively review your system's resource monitor (Task Manager/Activity Monitor, or a third-party tool) while using your primary AI/ML tools. Pay close attention to disk I/O (especially writes), CPU, and GPU usage to catch any unexpectedly high or sustained resource consumption.

Identify one small, repetitive task in your daily development workflow that takes more than 5 minutes. Spend 30-60 minutes this week automating it with a simple script (e.g., Python, Bash) or a macro. This could be anything from generating boilerplate code to running a series of build commands.

Consciously block out 20-30 minutes of 'unplugged' time (no screens, no tech) at least once or twice a week. Use this time for reflection on your projects, learning, and overall well-being. This helps combat burnout and provides mental space for deeper problem-solving and goal alignment.
